turn.user_message: Yes — put it into a plan
turn.context: Discharge sample conversation, turn 10 (playbook §7: a low-commitment trial, a threshold already met, a choice).

text: Start with a two-week trial on one ward. It needs no new staff and no new system. It tells us how much of the 5 hours comes back.
Hire the Discharge Manager now, not after the trial. Your own numbers are past both lines, so this is not a maybe-someday. They can run the trial.
chat.invite: Would you like me to plan the two-week trial, or first walk through what the full software does each day?
chat.note: Prove it on one ward, then grow it.

points.label: Cost against what is at stake

prompts: Why hire the manager before the trial ends?
What will the trial cost us?
chat.pointer: Pick a switch. The current runs to it, and the bulb lights at the last one.

blocks.title: Try it on one ward first
blocks.deck: Four switches, in order. Patients go home sooner only when every one is on.

source.label: Today
source.line: Ready at 10 AM, home at 3 PM

goal.label: Home hours sooner
goal.line: How many hours, the trial will show

steps.title: Start the trial on one ward
steps.line: The new order of steps, by hand. No new system.

steps.title: Measure the wait every day
steps.line: One person writes down the times for each patient.

steps.title: Decide using the numbers
steps.line: Spread it, or adjust and try again.

steps.title: Link the software, ward by ward
steps.line: Your IT team gives read-only access.

blocks.readout: The trial turns the biggest guess, how many hours come back, into a measured fact.

sheets.title: Start the trial on one ward
sheets.text: The trial runs the new order of steps by hand, so it needs no new system. One ward with a usual mix of patients.

lines.label: Cost
lines.value: No new staff, no new system

sheets.title: Measure the wait every day
sheets.text: Week 1 runs as usual and records the times. Week 2 runs the new order and records the same times.

lines.label: Who records
lines.value: The Discharge Manager, or a nurse

sheets.entry: Who could write the times down?

sheets.title: Decide using the numbers
sheets.text: We read the two weeks side by side. If the hours fell, we spread it. If not, we adjust and try again.
sheets.entry: Who should be in the room to decide?

sheets.title: Link the software, ward by ward
sheets.text: Once the order works by hand, the software takes over the writing. Your IT team gives read-only access.

lines.label: Needs
lines.value: One person in your IT team

sheets.entry: Who looks after your hospital software?

blocks.label: Hire the manager now
blocks.sub: 88% of beds in use against a line of 80%. 40 to 45 a day against a line of 40. Both are your numbers.
